title: Accounts Receivable Rule: Final Balance, Late Balance Charges and Closing of Entry & Patio Door Contracts
content:
Under Entry & Patio Door Contracts, the balance due on a door contract is the signed contract price plus the net contract charges minus the payments received net of refunds. Net contract charges are the change orders and fees added to the contract since signing, less the price credits granted against it. The result is rounded to the cent.

## Amount due at the end

The net charges of the contract's installation job (its Installation Jobs charges) are collected with it, so the amount due at the end is the balance due plus those job charges.

## Due date and recording

A door contract becomes installed when the installation of the contracted doors is completed and signed off on site; the date of that sign-off is the installation completion date.


The remaining balance falls due on the final balance due date, the stated number of calendar days after the installation completion date, and is recorded as a final balance payment when paid. For a financed contract, the lender funding is recorded as lender funding on the funding date and any remainder is paid by the customer.

## Late balance charge

- A door late balance charge applies only while the contract status is installed.
- A door late balance charge may be assessed only when the balance remains unpaid after the final balance due date, which falls the stated number of calendar days after the installation completion date.
- Calendar days are counted from the day after the installation completion date, and payment on the due date itself is on time.
- The late charge is the monthly rate times the unpaid balance, rounded to the cent, for each full 30-day period after the due date, never less than the minimum charge, assessed once at the end of each such period.

The contract status and the installation completion date are read from the contract record.

## Closing

The contract closes once it is installed and the balance due is zero; an overpayment at that point is refunded as an overpayment refund.

## Worked account (hypothetical, 5-day due period, 1.5% rate, $15.00 minimum)

- Signed contract price $6920.00; change orders $900.00 and a credit of $160.00 give net contract charges of $740.00; payments received net of refunds $5000.00. Balance due: $6920.00 plus $740.00 less $5000.00, that is $2660.00.
- Installation completed on 3 March. Counting from 4 March as day 1, day 5 is 8 March, the final balance due date. Payment on 8 March is on time.
- Still unpaid after 8 March with the contract installed: the first full 30-day period runs 9 March through 7 April, and one late charge is assessed at its end: 1.5% of $2660.00 is $39.90, above the $15.00 minimum, so the charge is $39.90.
- Had the unpaid balance been $700.00, 1.5% would be $10.50, and the charge for the period would be the $15.00 minimum.
- A contract that is not in status installed carries no late balance charge.
